\[
\boxed{\frac{5}{64}}
\]

For \(a>0\),
\[
A_N(a)=\sum_{k=0}^N\frac{(-1)^k\binom Nk}{k+a}
=\int_0^1 x^{a-1}(1-x)^N\,dx
=B(a,N+1)
=\frac{\Gamma(a)\Gamma(N+1)}{\Gamma(N+a+1)}.
\]

Let
\[
L=\log n,\qquad x=(b-a)L,\qquad q=e^x=n^{b-a}.
\]
Since \(b<a\), we have \(x<0\).

Uniformly for \(a\) in the fixed interval \((1/8,3/8)\),
\[
A_N(a)=\Gamma(a)N^{-a}\left(1-\frac{a(a+1)}{2N}+O(N^{-2})\right).
\]
Hence
\[
A_n(a)=\Gamma(a)n^{-a}\left(1-\frac{a(a+1)}{2n}+O(n^{-2})\right),
\]
while the correction terms in \(A_{n^2}\) and \(A_{n^3}\) are only \(O(n^{-2})\). Therefore
\[
T_n(a,b)=\Gamma(a)n^{-a}\left(1+q+q^2-\frac{a(a+1)}{2n}+O(n^{-2})\right).
\]

Next,
\[
\frac{A_{n^2+n}(a)}{A_{n^2}(a)}
=\prod_{j=1}^n\frac{n^2+j}{n^2+a+j}.
\]
Taking logarithms,
\[
\log\frac{A_{n^2+n}(a)}{A_{n^2}(a)}
=-\frac an+\frac{a}{2n^2}+O(n^{-3}),
\]
so
\[
1-\frac{A_{n^2+n}(a)}{A_{n^2}(a)}
=\frac an\left(1-\frac{a+1}{2n}+O(n^{-2})\right).
\]
Thus
\[
D_n(a,b)
=\Gamma(a)n^{-a}q\frac an
\left(1-\frac{a+1}{2n}+O(n^{-2})\right).
\]

So
\[
R_n(a,b)
=\frac{q}{n(1+q+q^2)}
\left(1+\frac1n c(a,x)+O(n^{-2})\right),
\]
where
\[
c(a,x)=\frac{a+1}{2}\left(\frac{a}{1+e^x+e^{2x}}-1\right).
\]
Therefore
\[
\log R_n(a,b)
=-L+g(x)+\frac1n c(a,x)+O(n^{-2}),
\]
with
\[
g(x)=x-\log(1+e^x+e^{2x}).
\]

Since \(x=(b-a)L\), differentiation with respect to \(a\) acts as
\[
\frac{\partial}{\partial a}=\partial_a-L\partial_x.
\]

At \(x=0\),
\[
g''(0)=-\frac23,\qquad g''''(0)=\frac23,
\]
and
\[
c_x(a,0)=-\frac{a(a+1)}6,\qquad
c_{xxx}(a,0)=\frac{a(a+1)}6,
\]
\[
c_a(a,0)=\frac{a-1}{3},\qquad
c_{axx}(a,0)=\frac{2a+1}{18}.
\]

The first derivative condition gives
\[
0=-Lg'(x)+\frac1n(c_a-Lc_x)+O\left(\frac{L}{n^2}\right).
\]
This forces \(x\to0\), and then
\[
x=\frac{x_0(a)}n+\frac{y(a)}{nL}+o\left(\frac1{nL}\right),
\]
with
\[
x_0(a)=-\frac{c_x(a,0)}{g''(0)}
=-\frac{a(a+1)}4,
\]
and
\[
y(a)=\frac{c_a(a,0)}{g''(0)}
=\frac{1-a}{2}.
\]

The third derivative condition gives
\[
0=-L^3g'''(x)+\frac1n\left(-L^3c_{xxx}+3L^2c_{axx}+O(L)\right).
\]
Using \(g'''(x)=g''''(0)x+O(x^2)\), its leading term again gives
\[
x_0(a)=-\frac{c_{xxx}(a,0)}{g''''(0)}
=-\frac{a(a+1)}4,
\]
and the next term gives
\[
y(a)=\frac{3c_{axx}(a,0)}{g''''(0)}
=\frac{2a+1}{4}.
\]

Thus both derivative conditions require
\[
\frac{1-a}{2}=\frac{2a+1}{4}.
\]
Hence
\[
2-2a=2a+1,
\qquad a\to\frac14.
\]

Finally,
\[
x=(b-a)L=-(a-b)L,
\]
so
\[
n(\log n)(a_n-b_n)=-nx.
\]
Since
\[
x=-\frac{a(a+1)}{4n}+o(n^{-1})
\]
and \(a_n\to1/4\),
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} n(\log n)(a_n-b_n)
=\frac{(1/4)(5/4)}4
=\frac{5}{64}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{5}{64}}
\]
